title: Throughput contract orchestrator and granular throttle tuner
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers running Dedicated clusters need stable per-tenant throughput guarantees while allowing controlled, short-lived overprovisioning for bursty workloads. Current autoscalers operate at pool granularity and produce coarse throttling that either wastes capacity or allows latency SLO violations. This PR introduces a throughput contract orchestrator (TCO) and a granular throttle tuner (GTT) to reconcile per-tenant throughput contracts with pool-level autoscaling and short-term oversubscription. Scope: orchestrator component that consumes reservation/commitment metadata and translates it into soft throughput contracts, a per-tenant throttle layer that applies sliding-window rate envelopes, telemetry exports that expose percentile-backed utilization and contract fulfillment, and a rollout plan with safety guards. Design summary: - Throughput Contract Orchestrator (pkg/contract): collects reservation state, linear-linked commitments, and runtime utilization signals to compute a prioritized set of active contracts. Contracts have three constraints: steady guarantee (long-window), burst allowance (short-window), and a degradation weight for proportional shedding. - Granular Throttle Tuner (pkg/throttle): attaches as a middleware before the serving gateway’s admission controller. Uses a token-bucket-ish envelope derived from an exponential moving quantile of recent throughput and contracts; supports dynamic debt accounting to allow short bursts while recording owed capacity. - Telemetry and reporting: emits contract_fulfillment{tenant}, contract_violation{tenant}, util_p50/p90/p99 per tenant, and contract_debt gauges. Adds an aggregated fanout endpoint (/internal/telemetry/contract-rollup) for downstream reporting and billing. - Safety and fallback: if contract inputs are stale or the orchestrator fails, throttle tuner falls back to conservative per-tenant floor derived from historical minima and signals fallback events to Sentry and the observability console. Checklist (all items are in a single contiguous description): [x] Compute contract model and prioritization rules; [x] Implement orchestrator reconcile loop with leader election; [x] Add throttle tuner with debt accounting and sliding windows; [x] Wire telemetry metrics and Prometheus exposition; [x] Add unit and integration tests for debt accounting and degradation flows; [x] Add canary rollout config and feature flag; [x] Update console to show per-tenant contract fulfillment metrics (frontend change behind flag); [x] Document behavior in docs/dedicated/throughput-contracts.md Testing: unit tests (pkg/contract/*, pkg/throttle/*) and integration scenarios that simulate tenants with constant baseline plus Poisson bursts. Ran local cluster e2e with a 3-node dedicated pool and synthetic tenants (1 steady, 2 bursty). Results: 1) average contract fulfillment improved from 87% -> 98% for high-priority tenants under the test workload, 2) observed 10-15% reduction in unnecessary autoscaler scale-ups because short bursts are absorbed by debt accounting, 3) tail latency for low-priority tenants increased marginally in sustained overload scenarios (within acceptable degradation weight). Rollout plan: enable behind feature flag, small canary on 5% of dedicated fleets for 48 hours, inspect contract_fulfillment and tail-latency dashboards, then progressive 25%/50%/100% rollout with automated rollback if contract_violation rate > 1% for high-priority tenants for > 30 minutes. Related work: builds on ENG-1532 (reservation ledger refactor) and references SUP-1147 for a customer incident that motivated per-tenant fairness. Impact: reduces churn from autoscaler thrashing and provides clearer billing signals for burst allowances. Operational notes: operators can tune short-window burst multiplier and degradation_weight in the TCO config. Security: no new surface for external traffic; telemetry endpoint is internal-only. Documentation: docs/dedicated/throughput-contracts.md added with configuration knobs and safety guidelines.

release_notes: Add throughput contract orchestrator and granular throttle tuner for Dedicated pools: - Per-tenant throughput contracts (steady guarantee + short burst allowance) - Debt-backed burst absorption to reduce autoscaler churn - New telemetry: contract_fulfillment, contract_violation, contract_debt and util_p50/p90/p99 - Feature-flagged rollout with canary and automated rollback conditions
notes_for_operators: Tunable knobs: TCO.short_window_mins (default 2), TCO.long_window_mins (default 60), TCO.degradation_weight (default per-tenant 1.0), throttle.debt_capacity_multiplier (default 1.5). If fallback events spike, disable feature flag and inspect orchestrator leader election logs and metrics/contract_rollup for stale inputs.
